"'''Give Me One Reason'''" is a song written and performed by American singer-songwriter [[Tracy Chapman]]. It was included on her fourth studio album, ''[[New Beginning (Tracy Chapman album)|New Beginning]]'' (1995), and was released as a single in various territories between November 1995 and March 1997, her first since 1992's "Dreaming on a World". The song is Chapman's biggest US hit, reaching number three on the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Billboard Hot 100|Hot 100]]. It is also her biggest hit in Australia, where it reached number three as well, and it topped the charts of Canada and Iceland. Elsewhere, the song reached number 16 in New Zealand, but it underperformed in the United Kingdom, peaking at number 95 in March 1997.

Chapman first performed "Give Me One Reason" during her 1988 tour, seven years before its release.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tracy Chapman Setlist at Rockefeller's, Houston, TX |url=https://www.setlist.fm/setlist/tracy-chapman/1988/rockefellers-houston-tx-2bc3e0d6.html |website=Setlist.fm |access-date=May 12, 2021}}</ref> She also performed the song on the December 16, 1989, episode of ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name="snl">{{cite web|url=http://snlarchives.net/Episodes/?198912166|title=SNL Archives {{!}} Episodes {{!}} December 16, 1989 #6|work=SNL Archives|last=Navaroli|first=Joel|accessdate=January 27, 2022}}</ref> Chapman earned the [[Grammy Award for Best Rock Song]] for the track, and it was also nominated for [[Grammy Award for Record of the Year|Record of the Year]], [[Grammy Award for Song of the Year|Song of the Year]], and [[Grammy Award for Best Female Rock Vocal Performance|Best Female Rock Vocal Performance]] at the [[39th Grammy Awards|Grammy Awards of 1997]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.grammy.com/artists/tracy-chapman/878|title=Tracy Chapman|publisher=[[Grammy Award]]s|access-date=August 8, 2021}}</ref> A version of this song featuring [[Eric Clapton]] was included on the 1999 compilation album ''[[A Very Special Christmas Live]]''. A music video was released to promote the single.

"Give Me One Reason" is a song written and performed by American singer-songwriter Tracy Chapman. It was included on her fourth studio album, New Beginning (1995), and was released as a single in various territories between November 1995 and March 1997, her first since 1992's "Dreaming on a World". The song is Chapman's biggest US hit, reaching number three on the Billboard Hot 100. It is also her biggest hit in Australia, where it reached number three as well, and it topped the charts of Canada and Iceland. Elsewhere, the song reached number 16 in New Zealand, but it underperformed in the United Kingdom, peaking at number 95 in March 1997.

Chapman first performed "Give Me One Reason" during her 1988 tour, seven years before its release. She also performed the song on the December 16, 1989, episode of Saturday Night Live. Chapman earned the Grammy Award for Best Rock Song for the track, and it was also nominated for Record of the Year, Song of the Year, and Best Female Rock Vocal Performance at the Grammy Awards of 1997. A version of this song featuring Eric Clapton was included on the 1999 compilation album A Very Special Christmas Live. A music video was released to promote the single.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: Alan Jones from ''[[Music Week]]'' wrote, "Less intense and somewhat looser than her benchmark hit [[Fast Car]], it perfectly mixes her folksy style with traditional [[R&B]] qualities, intelligent lyrics and that edgy distinctive voice. Compelling listening."<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Alan|last=Jones|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/UK/Music-Week/1997/Music-Week-1997-03-22.pdf|title=Talking Music|magazine=[[Music Week]]|date=March 22, 1997|page=8|accessdate=May 13, 2022}}</ref> ''[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]]'' said the song was, "strutting along a plucked, head-nodding guitar melody and Chapman’s grainy alto. Centering on an imbalanced relationship, each verse grows more frustrated from a lack of reciprocity; then the band kicks in and the pleading in her voice becomes cathartic, begging for a reason to stay while knowing it won’t come."<ref>{{cite web|title=The 250 Best Songs of the 1990s|url=https://pitchfork.com/features/lists-and-guides/the-best-songs-of-the-1990s/|work=[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]]|author=Eric Torres|date=September 27, 2022 }}</ref> In June 2026, [[CBS News]] included the song in its list of the 250 essential American songs of the past 250 years, one of two Chapman songs to make the list.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Essential American Songbook |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/projects/2026/sunmo-american-songbook/ |access-date=2026-06-30 |website=www.cbsnews.com |language=en}}</ref>

sections.heading: Cover versions
sections.wikitext: In 2015, [[Kelly Clarkson]] covered the song for [[SiriusXM]], garnering over 2.5 million views.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kelly Clarkson - "Give Me One Reason" (Tracy Chapman Cover) [LIVE @ SiriusXM] | date=March 18, 2015 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JN66KH4lr0I |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/JN66KH4lr0I |archive-date=December 21, 2021 |url-status=live |via=YouTube|access-date=September 30, 2021}}{{cbignore}}</ref> She again covered the song for her talk show, ''[[The Kelly Clarkson Show]]'', in 2021.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Weisholtz |first1=Drew |title=Kelly Clarkson brings down the house with cover of 'Give Me One Reason' |url=https://www.today.com/popculture/kelly-clarkson-covers-tracy-chapman-s-give-me-one-reason-t206122 |website=Today |date=January 19, 2021 |publisher=The Today Show |access-date=September 30, 2021}}</ref> The band [[Ruth (band)|Ruth]] covered the song on their 2009 digitally released ''The Covers EP''. In 2021, [[Black Stone Cherry]] released two versions of the song on the deluxe edition of their album ''[[The Human Condition (Black Stone Cherry album)|The Human Condition]]''. Their versions peaked at number 25 on ''Billboard''{{'}}s Mainstream Rock Airplay chart.<ref name=Billboard>{{cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/black-stone-cherry/chart-history/rtt/|title=Chart History: Black Stone Cherry (Mainstream Rock Airplay)|publisher=billboard.com|access-date=April 16, 2021}}</ref>
sections.text: In 2015, Kelly Clarkson covered the song for SiriusXM, garnering over 2.5 million views. She again covered the song for her talk show, The Kelly Clarkson Show, in 2021. The band Ruth covered the song on their 2009 digitally released The Covers EP. In 2021, Black Stone Cherry released two versions of the song on the deluxe edition of their album The Human Condition. Their versions peaked at number 25 on Billboard{{'}}s Mainstream Rock Airplay chart.
